guide.p: Health questions often ask about lifestyle (diet, exercise, stress), healthcare (who should pay, prevention or treatment) and ageing populations. These words help you discuss both personal habits and public policy.

bullets: Learn words in phrases, not alone: notice which verbs, adjectives and prepositions go with them.
Practise each word in a sentence about your own life or country — it will be easier to use in Speaking.
In Writing, choose the precise word over the impressive-sounding one. Accuracy beats complexity.

guide.tip: 'Healthy' describes a person, food or lifestyle; 'healthcare' is the system of medical services; 'health' is the general condition.

vocab.meaning: a way of life with little physical activity
vocab.example: Office work often leads to a sedentary lifestyle.

vocab.meaning: a diet with the right amounts of different foods
vocab.example: A balanced diet includes plenty of vegetables.

vocab.meaning: containing substances the body needs
vocab.example: School meals should be cheap and nutritious.

vocab.meaning: food changed by industrial methods, often with added salt or sugar
vocab.example: Processed food is linked to heart disease.

vocab.meaning: the condition of being very overweight
vocab.example: Childhood obesity has doubled in some countries.

vocab.meaning: the average number of years a person is expected to live
vocab.example: Life expectancy has risen steadily for decades.

vocab.meaning: lasting a long time (of illness)
vocab.example: Diabetes is a chronic condition.

vocab.meaning: intended to stop something happening
vocab.example: Preventive care is cheaper than treatment.

vocab.meaning: giving a substance to protect against a disease
vocab.example: Vaccination programmes have saved millions of lives.

vocab.meaning: the condition of a person's mind and emotions
vocab.example: Exercise has clear benefits for mental health.

vocab.meaning: the state of being healthy and happy
vocab.example: Green spaces improve residents' wellbeing.

vocab.meaning: mental pressure caused by difficulties
vocab.example: Long working hours cause stress and poor sleep.

vocab.meaning: a heavy responsibility or cost
vocab.example: An ageing population places a burden on health services.

vocab.meaning: a population with a growing share of older people
vocab.example: An ageing population needs more care workers.

vocab.meaning: the services and organisations that provide medical care
vocab.example: The country's healthcare system is funded by taxes.

vocab.meaning: an organised effort to improve health habits
vocab.example: A public health campaign encouraged people to stop smoking.

vocab.meaning: a sign of an illness
vocab.example: Fever is a common symptom of flu.

vocab.meaning: identifying an illness
vocab.example: Early diagnosis improves the chances of recovery.

vocab.meaning: an unwanted effect of a medicine
vocab.example: Drowsiness is a side effect of some medicines.

vocab.meaning: to become healthy again after an illness
vocab.example: It took him months to recover from the operation.

vocab.meaning: not getting enough sleep
vocab.example: Sleep deprivation reduces concentration.

vocab.meaning: to exercise, especially in a gym
vocab.example: I try to work out three times a week.

vocab.meaning: the ability to get medical services
vocab.example: Rural areas often have poor access to healthcare.

vocab.meaning: physically fit
vocab.example: Cycling to work keeps me in good shape.
